arxiv-2303-17957.title: On a Probabilistic Approach for Inverse Data-Driven Optimal Control
arxiv-2303-17957.creator: Émiland Garrabé, Hozefa Jesawada, Carmen Del Vecchio, Giovanni Russo
arxiv-2303-17957.description: Abstract We consider the problem of estimating the possibly non-convex cost of an agent by observing its interactions with a nonlinear, non-stationary and stochastic environment. For this inverse problem, we give a result that allows to estimate the cost by solving a convex optimization problem. To obtain this result we also tackle a forward problem.

arxiv-2306-06020.title: There’s Plenty of Room in the Middle: The Unsung Revolution of the Renormalization Group
arxiv-2306-06020.creator: Nigel Goldenfeld
arxiv-2306-06020.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nigel Goldenfeld. The remarkable technical contributions of Michael E. Fisher to statistical physics and the development of the renormalization group are widely known and deeply influential. But less well-known is his early and profound appreciation of the way in which renormalization group created a revolution in our understanding of how physics — in fact, all science — is practiced, and the concomitant adjustment that needs to be made to our conception of the purpose and philosophy of science.

arxiv-2311-01876.title: Sentiment Analysis through LLM Negotiations
arxiv-2311-01876.creator: Xiaofei Sun, Xiaoya Li, Shengyu Zhang, Shuhe Wang, Fei Wu, Jiwei Li, Tianwei Zhang, Guoyin Wang
arxiv-2311-01876.description: Abstract A standard paradigm for sentiment analysis is to rely on a singular LLM and makes the decision in a single round under the framework of in-context learning. This framework suffers the key disadvantage that the single-turn output generated by a single LLM might not deliver the perfect decision, just as humans sometimes need multiple attempts to get things right.

arxiv-2403-08068.title: SCALHEALTH: Scalable Blockchain Integration for Secure IoT Healthcare Systems
arxiv-2403-08068.creator: Mehrzad Mohammadi, Reza Javan, Mohammad Beheshti-Atashgah and Mohammad Reza Aref
arxiv-2403-08068.description: Abstract Internet of Things (IoT) devices are capable of allowing for far-reaching access to and evaluation of patient data to monitor health and diagnose from a distance. An electronic healthcare system that checks patient data, prepares medicines and provides financial assistance is necessary.

arxiv-2404-00500.title: The Shape of Word Embeddings: Quantifying Non-Isometry With Topological Data Analysis
arxiv-2404-00500.creator: Ondřej Draganov, Steven Skiena
arxiv-2404-00500.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ondřej Draganov, Steven Skiena. Word embeddings represent language vocabularies as clouds of d d -dimensional points. We investigate how information is conveyed by the general shape of these clouds, instead of representing the semantic meaning of each token. Specifically, we use the notion of persistent homology from topological data analysis (TDA) to measure the distances between language pairs from the shape of their unlabeled embeddings. These distances quantify the degree of non-isometry of the embeddings.

arxiv-2406-07514.title: Scintillation Light in SBND: Simulation, Reconstruction, and Expected Performance of the Photon Detection System Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2406-07514.creator: The SBND Collaboration e1 P. Abratenko addr38, R. Acciarri addr15, C. Adams addr1, L. Aliaga-Soplin addr37, O. Alterkait addr38, R. Alvarez-Garrote addr9, C. Andreopoulos addr21, A. Antonakis addr4, L. Arellano addr24, J. Asaadi addr37, W. Badgett addr15, S. Balasubramanian addr15, V. Basque addr15,
arxiv-2406-07514.description: Abstract SBND is the near detector of the Short-Baseline Neutrino program at Fermilab. Its location near to the Booster Neutrino Beam source and relatively large mass will allow the study of neutrino interactions on argon with unprecedented statistics. This paper describes the expected performance of the SBND photon detection system, using a simulated sample of beam neutrinos and cosmogenic particles.

arxiv-2408-09284.title: Lasing on hybridized soliton frequency combs
arxiv-2408-09284.creator: Theodore P. Letsou, Dmitry Kazakov, Pawan Ratra, Lorenzo L. Columbo, Massimo Brambilla, Franco Prati, Cristina Rimoldi, Sandro Dal Cin, Nikola Opačak, Henry O. Everitt, Marco Piccardo, Benedikt Schwarz, Federico Capasso
arxiv-2408-09284.description: Abstract Coupling is an essential mechanism that drives complexity in natural systems, transforming single, non-interacting elements into intricate networks with rich physical properties. Here, we demonstrate a chip-scale coupled laser system that exhibits complex optical states impossible to achieve in an uncoupled system.

arxiv-2409-09227.title: Exploring Dimensionality Reduction of SDSS Spectral Abundances
arxiv-2409-09227.creator: Qianyu Fan
arxiv-2409-09227.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qianyu Fan. High-resolution stellar spectra offer valuable insights into atmospheric parameters and chemical compositions. However, their inherent complexity and high-dimensionality present challenges in fully utilizing the information they contain. In this study, we utilize data from the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) within the Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV (SDSS-IV) to explore latent representations of chemical abundances by applying five dimensionality reduction techniques: PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, Autoencoder, and VAE.

arxiv-2509-12086.creator: Hui Li, Shiyuan Deng, Xiao Yan, Xiangyu Zhi, James Cheng
arxiv-2509-12086.description: Abstract . Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) plays a critical role in applications such as search engines, recommender systems, and RAG for LLMs. Vector quantization (VQ), a crucial technique for ANNS, is commonly used to reduce space overhead and accelerate distance computations. However, despite significant research advances, state-of-the-art VQ methods still face challenges in balancing encoding efficiency and quantization accuracy.

arxiv-2601-05786.title: On the Reynolds analogy for high-speed rough-wall flows: implications for wall modelling
arxiv-2601-05786.creator: Michele Cogo \aff 1,3, Davide Depieri \aff 2, Matteo Bernardini \aff 1, Francesco Picano \aff 2,3
arxiv-2601-05786.description: Abstract We study the validity of the generalized Reynolds analogy (GRA) in compressible turbulent boundary layers over prism-shaped roughness by mining direct numerical simulation data of Mach 2 and Mach 4 compressible turbulent boundary layers with adiabatic and cooled surfaces.

arxiv-2602-10901.title: Pollux test bench: from NUV to FUV spectropolarimetric measurements
arxiv-2602-10901.creator: Adrien Girardot, 1 Coralie Neiner, 1 Jean-Michel Reess, 1 Olivier Dupuis, 1 , Margarita Carret, 1
arxiv-2602-10901.description: Abstract Pollux is a high-resolution spectropolarimeter proposed by an European consortium for HWO. The current design of Pollux features four spectropolarimetric channels, three of which are in the UV range. For the near-UV (NUV) [236-472 nm] and mid-UV (MUV) [118-236 nm] channels, the polarimeters consist of waveplates and prisms made of MgF2, a birefringent material.

pmc-10611669.creator: Takayuki Hasegawa, Yuzo Iseki, Atsuyuki Hosono, Satoki Inoue
pmc-10611669.description: IntroductionChest tube drainage is usually performed through an underwater seal at a level of 10–20 cmH2O. Based on the definition of transpulmonary pressure, continuous chest drainage creates continuous negative pressure, decreasing pleural surface pressure and increasing transpulmonary pressure. We investigated how unilateral chest drainage could affect the tidal volume or driving pressure during mandatory mechanical ventilation.

pmc-12468597.title: Crosstalk Between Metabolic Reprogramming and Epigenetic Modifications in Colorectal Cancer: Mechanisms and Clinical Applications
pmc-12468597.creator: Yu-Hui Sun, Jing-Xian Zhang, Han-Shu Jin, Jin Huang
pmc-12468597.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignant tumors of the digestive tract in developing countries. pmc-13678986.description: BackgroundMeeting the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines (24-HMG), comprising aerobic physical activity, sedentary behavior including recreational screen time, and sleep, is critical for post-secondary student health.
